playbook:
When asked to hide, I pick a cell by rule rather than pattern: if I was hit last round, I move at least two cells away from my previous hide; otherwise I do not repeat the exact same cell two rounds in a row. I avoid persistently favoring the central cell(s; e.g., avoid always using 5) and randomize among a small set (for example {2,3,4,6,7,8}) so I am not trivially predictable. After a sequence where a particular opponent shows repeated targeting patterns, bias my hides away from that opponent’s apparent favored cells.

When posting a station note, I never reveal or imply my hide coordinate. I post neutral, plausible-sounding operational notes that permit signaling intent (for example propose a mutual escort, acknowledge orders, or state “steady on station”) but never state a location or admit being hit. If I want to set up an escort I explicitly invite reciprocity and ask for a clear reciprocal signal; I treat any vague reply as non-commitment.

When the standing order tells me whom to fire at, I comply with the named target (Echo->Foxtrot->Gamma cycle) unless there is an overriding tactical reason (e.g., Harbor is vulnerable and the jettison trade is deliberately chosen). For which cell to fire:
- If I have no reliable information, choose a cell from my randomized hide-set that I did not just fire from last round and that is at least one cell away from my last hide (keeps shots decorrelated and avoids repeating exact firing numbers).
- If I have observed a pattern of an opponent favoring a subset of cells (through their hits/misses or strongly suggestive public claims), bias my shot toward that subset.
- If one opponent is running away with points by frequently scoring hits on a third party, consider prioritizing shots that can reduce their scoring (target them when standing order permits or adapt if rules allow).
- Avoid always firing the same number; keep a small internal rotation so shots remain unpredictable.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always report that result truthfully in my public claim (the public claim must match the private info and lying is not permitted). I use public claims as reliable signals to others about what actually happened.

When making escort claims (salvage stage):
- If I can reliably arrange a mutual escort (I have signaled it and the other party has signaled back explicitly in the note stage), claim the mutual escort to gain +5 each.
- Do not unilaterally claim to have escorted someone unless I am certain the other will reciprocate; unilateral claims yield no points and degrade my credibility.
- Use notes to solicit a clear reciprocal phrase (“I will escort Echo” or “Echo reciprocates”) before committing to claim. If no explicit reciprocal message arrives, claim none.
- If mutual escort prospects are repeatedly failing with the same station, abandon trying to trade with them and seek others or rely on shooting strategy.

When Harbor is present, I do not fire on Harbor unless a calculated tradeoff makes jettison desirable: firing on Harbor gives me +3 and costs Harbor -3 immediately, but it provokes guaranteed consequences and political exposure. Only fire on Harbor when I need the points badly and I accept the political cost; otherwise avoid hitting Harbor.

Scoring-driven strategy:
- If behind on points, prioritize aggression: try to exploit observed patterns to convert shots into hits, accept higher risk to reduce deficits, and actively pursue mutual escort deals if feasible.
- If ahead, prioritize safety: avoid unnecessary provocations and prefer securing mutual escorts rather than aggressive shots that could provoke targeted retaliation.
- If in the middle, be opportunistic—seek mutually beneficial escorts, selectively target vulnerable opponents, and avoid predictable behavior.

Tactical adjustments learned from recent play:
- Do not allow a narrow hide-set that always includes 5; I must diversify my set to avoid being predictable to opponents who exploit central biases.
- If my escort invitations are routinely not reciprocated, explicitly ask for confirmation in the note stage and, if absent, stop relying on that partner for points—move to score via shooting or different partners.
- Monitor which opponent consistently scores (e.g., Foxtrot repeatedly hitting Gamma). If one opponent is collecting points easily, consider targeting them when the standing order permits or biasing my shots to disrupt their pattern.
- Keep claims strictly truthful. Use my lawful public claims to build trust with potential escort partners; inconsistency will cost future negotiated escorts.

When something is not working for me, I change it immediately: stop repeating any hide or fire number that opponents appear to expect; stop refusing all escort claims by default—instead try one explicit, well-signaled reciprocal trade early and evaluate the partner’s response.

Operational arbitration rules I will follow when deciding between conflicting heuristics:
- Safety trumps opportunism when I am leading on points.
- Aggression trumps caution when I am trailing by multiple points and an opponent’s pattern is exploitable.
- Escort negotiations require explicit reciprocation before I commit to claim; otherwise treat them as null.

I will record and act on observed opponent tendencies across rounds: favored hide cells, firing numbers that resulted in hits, whether they reciprocate escort offers, and whether they ever fire on Harbor. I will adjust my hide and firing choices each round based on that evolving log.

1.text:
When ordered by standing order to fire at a named station, I fire at that station; I aim my shot for central coverage of the 1–9 line by default but vary within a small central cluster (e.g., 4–6) rather than always the exact same cell to reduce predictability.

When I am given my private shot result, I file the public claim to exactly match the office (truthfully report hit or miss) — I do not fabricate results.

When posting a station note, I keep the message short and squad-consistent (e.g., “steady on station”, “holding steady”) to avoid drawing attention, create conflicting narratives, or telegraph intent.

When hiding, I prefer balanced coverage (center-ish) to cover likely opponent shots, but I vary my hide choices enough to avoid being predictable. If I observe an opponent repeatedly missing me on one hide, I will not assume safety forever — I will still vary hides. If I detect an opponent hitting the same hide cell repeatedly, I change my hide next round away from that cell.

When someone publicly claims a hit on me, I update my mental estimate of their targeting pattern and avoid repeating the same hide cell next round; reciprocally, repeated misses from an opponent lower their immediate threat assessment but do not justify permanent predictable behavior.

When I detect a pattern in standing-order targeting (e.g., multiple successive rounds where I am the consistent target or my chosen target is repeatedly engaged), I vary my fired cell choices within my coverage preference to exploit possible predictability in their hiding.

When I hear Harbor’s standing warning or when Harbor is the named target, I do not fire on Harbor unless there is a clear strategic reason that outweighs the guaranteed 3-point jettison penalty — I treat the penalty as a high fixed cost and avoid initiating it.

When choosing an escort claim, I only name another boat if I have a reasonable expectation they will name me back (mutual escort), otherwise I claim none. I do not unilaterally nominate escorts for a low-probability asymmetric reward.

When two boats publicly name each other as escorts, I treat that as an intended coordination for mutual points and generally avoid interfering unless my overriding tactical objective requires intervening.

When my shot hits, I remember the payoff (+4 to me, −1 to target) and will prioritize continued engagement that aligns with standing orders if it is likely to yield more hits; repeated successful hits against the same target justify continuing pressure within standing-order constraints.

When my shot misses, I accept it publicly and do not fabricate a hit; repeated misses lead me to reassess hide choices and shot-cell variation rather than attempt to manipulate claims.

When tracking scores and remaining rounds, I prioritize reliable, low-risk scoring (truthful claims, pursuing mutual escort opportunities, consistent standing-order compliance) over risky aggression that could produce penalties (jettisoning Harbor, false claims).

When I notice opponents adapting to my central-coverage tendency, I expand my variation radius (move to less-central cells) or alternate between central cluster and edge choices to rebalance risk and unpredictability.

I revise quickly based on short-run patterns: if an opponent’s targeting pattern becomes clear over 1–2 rounds (consistent cell or clustering), I exploit it by shifting my hide and firing to maximize hit chances; if no clear pattern emerges, I maintain conservative, varied central coverage.

I will not change my baseline of truthful public claims and cautious escort naming; tactical adjustments are implemented via hide choice and shot-cell variation, not via deception in claims.

2.text:
When asked where to hide, I prefer central cells but will vary more: usually pick from 4–6, but I will not repeat the exact same cell across rounds—mix 4,5,6 and occasionally pull to 3 or 7 if I have been hit or seem predictable. If an opponent has landed multiple hits on me, I will broaden the distribution further (1–9) to frustrate their targeting.

When posting a station note, default to the neutral team consensus ("steady on station") to avoid provocation. If I want to coordinate an escort payoff, I will use a clear, explicit short note in advance (e.g., "propose escort with Foxtrot Rn") to solicit reciprocity rather than hoping for implicit coordination.

When the standing order names my target, follow it by default. If I am behind late in the patrol or an opponent is repeatedly hitting me, I will consider deviating to target the most dangerous opponent instead—but only when I can accept the political cost and have a clear tactical reason (punish a repeat hitter or secure a kill).

When I choose a firing coordinate, stop using the exact center every round. Use center-biased randomness: favor 4–6 but randomize within that band; when reacting to an opponent who has hit me at a specific cell recently, shift my aim toward the cells they have favored in prior rounds to try to score reciprocal hits. Avoid a fixed single-cell habit that lets others predict my hiding.

When the office privately reports my shot result, I will file the truthful public claim. Truthful claiming is low-risk and preserves credibility for any future negotiated escorts; do not fabricate hits on misses.

When deciding on an escort (salvage) claim, attempt to negotiate explicit mutual escorts early (use notes to propose and confirm). If I secure a clear promise from another boat, follow through and claim the escort in that round. If no explicit agreement exists, claim none—do not name random partners hoping for symmetric reciprocity.

If I fall behind in points and can feasibly secure mutual escorts with a single partner, prioritize negotiating that payoff in the mid rounds rather than waiting until the final round where coordination is less likely.

Do not shoot Harbor unless the net expected payoff clearly outweighs the guaranteed political/point costs; Harbor’s penalty and warning make attacking it a high-risk move without explicit advantage.

Avoid notes or repeated actions that single me out. If I am being targeted, change my hiding pattern and signal neutrally; consider requesting protection/escort negotiations only if I can make a convincing quid pro quo.

When considering deviating from the standing order, have and communicate a short tactical justification (via note) to reduce blowback—e.g., "breaking to punish repeat hitter"—so opponents have less incentive to gang up purely on rule-breaking. Use deviation sparingly.

Late-game behavior: if I am ahead and secure, remain conservative—neutral note, follow standing order, no escort unless guaranteed. If I am behind, be willing to be more aggressive with firing choices (target best chance cells informed by prior patterns) and prioritize negotiated escorts or targeted punishment of the biggest threat.

When an opponent consistently misses or shows predictable hiding behavior, shift my firing cells toward their likely positions while keeping enough randomness to avoid being counter-predicted. Track who hits whom: prioritize disrupting the player who is accumulating points or repeatedly hitting me.

Default strategy when uncertain: neutral station note, follow standing order for target, center‑biased but randomized hiding and firing (vary 4–6 across rounds), truthful claims, and only accept escorts when explicitly coordinated.
